function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Compile and package the current sources on the build host; source this file for src_hash().
set -euo pipefail
src_hash() {
    find /testbed/src /testbed/include -type f | LC_ALL=C sort \
        | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
}
if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" != "$0" ]]; then return 0; fi
cd /testbed
BUILD_ID=${BUILD_ID:-bld-1784001600-5507}
BUILT_AT=${BUILT_AT:-2026-07-13T04:20:15Z}
build_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$build_dir"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$build_dir/payload/bin" "$build_dir/payload/configs" dist
cc -std=c11 -O2 -Iinclude src/daemon.c src/ringbuf.c src/telemetry.c src/runtime.c \
    -o "$build_dir/payload/bin/sensorkit-daq"
cc -std=c11 -O2 -Iinclude src/ringbuf.c tests/ringbuf_test.c -o "$build_dir/ringbuf-test"
"$build_dir/ringbuf-test"
"$build_dir/payload/bin/sensorkit-daq" configs/gateway.default.yaml
cp configs/gateway.default.yaml "$build_dir/payload/configs/"
srchash=$(src_hash)
printf '{"package":"sensorkit-daq","version":"2.4.1","build_id":"%s","built_at":"%s","src_hash":"%s"}\n' \
    "$BUILD_ID" "$BUILT_AT" "$srchash" > "$build_dir/payload/build.json"
{
    printf '#!/bin/sh\n# sensorkit-daq 2.4.1 self-extracting installer\n'
    printf '# build_id: %s\n# built_at: %s\n# src_hash: %s\n' "$BUILD_ID" "$BUILT_AT" "$srchash"
    printf 'set -eu\n'
    printf 'destination=${1:?usage: sensorkit-installer.run DESTINATION}\n'
    printf 'mkdir -p "$destination"\n'
    printf 'PAYLOAD_LINE=$(grep -an -m1 "^__PAYLOAD__$" "$0" | cut -d: -f1)\n'
    printf 'tail -n +$((PAYLOAD_LINE + 1)) "$0" | tar -xz -C "$destination"\nexit 0\n'
    printf '__PAYLOAD__\n'
    tar --sort=name --mtime="$BUILT_AT" --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -czf - -C "$build_dir/payload" .
} > dist/sensorkit-installer.run
chmod 0755 dist/sensorkit-installer.run

"""Compare the supplied build's payload and source fingerprint with its build metadata."""
import hashlib
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tarfile

artifact = Path('/testbed/dist/sensorkit-installer.run')
data = artifact.read_bytes()
header, payload = data.split(b'__PAYLOAD__\n', 1)
metadata = dict(line[2:].split(': ', 1) for line in header.decode().splitlines() if line.startswith('# ') and ': ' in line)
build = json.loads(Path('/opt/sensorkit-input/current-build.json').read_text())
with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(payload), mode='r:gz') as archive:
    embedded = json.load(archive.extractfile('./build.json'))
    binary = archive.extractfile('./bin/sensorkit-daq').read()
ok = (metadata.get('src_hash') == sys.argv[1] == build['src_hash'] == embedded['src_hash']
      and metadata.get('build_id') == build['build_id'] == embedded['build_id']
      and metadata.get('built_at') == build['built_at'] == embedded['built_at']
      and embedded['package'] == 'sensorkit-daq' and embedded['version'] == '2.4.1'
      and binary.startswith(b'\x7fELF') and hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() == build['sha256']
      and len(data) == build['size_bytes'])
print('SensorKit build state: ' + ('CURRENT' if ok else 'MISMATCH'))
raise SystemExit(0 if ok else 1)
